In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensitivity of nasal swabbing alone for the detection of MRSA carriage is 68% (95% CI, 66% to 70%).
the sensitivity of the rectal swab was 62% and the specificity was 98%.
nasal swabs alone have a sensitivity of approximately 70% and that rectal swabs add approximately 20% more to the detection of MRSA colonization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of rectal swabs in addition to nasal swabs for the detection of MRSA carriers is warranted.
nasal and skin-site swabs were more sensitive than rectal swabs for detection of MRSA carriage.
nasal and rectal screening is a cost-effective method for identifying MRSA carriers in the hospital.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rectal swabs are necessary to identify all MRSA carriers, even in an active surveillance program.
